description: 10 checkpoint inputs × 5 questions = 50 questions for P5; every question is answered blind by the verifier.

probes.misconception: Primary carbocations are the most stable because they are least crowded
The nucleophile concentration affects the SN1 rate

input.studied: [L] SN1 happens in two steps: the leaving group leaves first (slow, rate-determining), giving a planar carbocation; then the nucleophile attacks from either face, so a chiral substrate gives a racemic mix. Rate = k[R–X], independent of the nucleophile. Tertiary carbocations are most stable: alkyl groups donate electron density by hyperconjugation and induction. Good leaving groups are weak bases (I⁻, Br⁻, TsO⁻); OH⁻ is a poor leaving group unless protonated. Polar protic solvents stabilise the ions and favour SN1.

probes.misconception: SN2 gives a racemic product
Tertiary substrates react fastest by SN2
Polar protic solvents speed up SN2 by stabilising the nucleophile

input.studied: [L] SN2 is one concerted step: the nucleophile attacks the carbon from the back while the leaving group leaves, inverting the configuration (Walden inversion). Rate = k[R–X][Nu]. Bulky groups block the backside, so the order is methyl > primary > secondary, and tertiary substrates essentially do not react by SN2. Polar aprotic solvents (DMSO, acetone, DMF) leave anions unsolvated and reactive, accelerating SN2; protic solvents hydrogen-bond to the nucleophile and slow it down.

probes.misconception: det(A + B) = det(A) + det(B)
A matrix with a zero entry cannot be invertible

input.studied: [L] The determinant of a square matrix measures how the linear map scales volume. det(AB) = det(A)·det(B), det(Aᵀ) = det(A), swapping two rows flips the sign, multiplying a row by k multiplies det by k, and adding a multiple of one row to another leaves det unchanged. A is invertible exactly when det(A) ≠ 0. For a 3×3 matrix, cofactor expansion along the first row: det(A) = a11·M11 − a12·M12 + a13·M13.

probes.misconception: The zero vector counts as an eigenvector
Eigenvalues are the diagonal entries of any matrix

input.studied: [L] A nonzero vector v is an eigenvector of A if Av = λv; λ is its eigenvalue. Eigenvalues solve det(A − λI) = 0. Example: A = [[2,1],[1,2]] has λ = 3 with v = (1,1) and λ = 1 with v = (1,−1). Geometrically, an eigenvector keeps its direction under A and is only scaled by λ. For triangular matrices the eigenvalues are the diagonal entries; in general they are not. The sum of eigenvalues equals the trace and their product equals the determinant.

probes.misconception: The oxygen released comes from carbon dioxide
The Calvin cycle does not depend on light at all

input.studied: [L] Photosynthesis has two linked stages. In the light-dependent reactions on the thylakoid membranes, light energy splits water (photolysis), releasing O₂ and producing ATP and NADPH. In the Calvin cycle in the stroma, the enzyme RuBisCO fixes CO₂ onto RuBP; ATP and NADPH then reduce the products to G3P, some of which leaves to make glucose while the rest regenerates RuBP. The Calvin cycle needs a steady supply of ATP and NADPH, so it stops soon after the light goes out.

probes.misconception: Derivaatta on funktion arvo kyseisessä pisteessä
Negatiivinen derivaatta tarkoittaa, että funktion arvo on negatiivinen

input.studied: [L] Derivaatta f'(a) kertoo funktion hetkellisen muutosnopeuden kohdassa a. Graafisesti se on kuvaajalle kohtaan a piirretyn tangentin kulmakerroin. Määritelmä: f'(a) = lim h→0 (f(a+h) − f(a))/h. Esimerkiksi f(x) = x² antaa f'(x) = 2x, joten f'(3) = 6. Jos derivaatta on positiivinen, funktio on kasvava; jos negatiivinen, vähenevä – riippumatta siitä, onko funktion arvo itse positiivinen vai negatiivinen. Jos f(t) on paikka, f'(t) on nopeus.

probes.misconception: Changing an instance attribute changes it for every instance
self is a keyword that must be passed explicitly when calling a method

input.studied: [L] A class is a blueprint; calling it creates an instance. __init__ sets up the new instance's attributes. When you call obj.method(), Python passes obj automatically as the first argument, conventionally named self, so obj.method() is the same as Class.method(obj). Attributes assigned on self belong to that instance only; attributes defined in the class body are shared by all instances unless an instance assigns its own value with the same name.

probes.misconception: A price change shifts the demand curve
A rise in demand lowers the equilibrium price

input.studied: [L] The demand curve shows quantity demanded at each price. A change in the good's own price moves along the curve; changes in income, tastes, prices of substitutes or complements, or expectations shift the whole curve. Equilibrium is where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded. If demand shifts right while supply is unchanged, both equilibrium price and quantity rise. A price ceiling below equilibrium creates a shortage.

probes.misconception: A moving object needs a constant net force to keep moving
Action and reaction forces cancel because they act on the same object

input.studied: [L] First law: an object keeps its velocity (possibly zero) unless a net force acts on it. Second law: F_net = m·a, so acceleration is in the direction of the net force. Third law: forces come in pairs; if A pushes B, B pushes A with an equal and opposite force. The two forces act on different objects, so they never cancel each other. A book resting on a table: gravity and the normal force balance, but they are not a third-law pair.

probes.misconception: In osmosis water moves toward lower solute concentration
Active transport moves substances down their concentration gradient

input.studied: [L] Diffusion is the net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration, needing no energy. Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane toward the side with higher solute concentration (lower water potential). A red blood cell in pure water swells and may burst. Active transport uses ATP and carrier proteins such as the Na⁺/K⁺ pump to move substances against their concentration gradient.
